transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05 16:00 PT
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Tom Hsu (Redwood Solutions), Jordan Lee (Arclight Head of Infra), Maya Patel (Arclight Partnerships), Diego Alvarez (CTO), Sofia Gomez (Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um, we'll run about 30-45 minutes and, uh, aim to cover partner fit, what your fleet looks like, and potential pilot options. Priya's on to cover technical q's.
[00:18] Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks Alex. Quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, I run infra at Arclight. We sell GPU-backed edge racks and also operate a hybrid cloud offering. Maya: hi everyone.
[00:30] Priya: great thanks. can you give us a sense of your current customers and what workloads are most common? language models, embeddings, etc.
[00:45] Jordan: Mostly LLM inference, mix of 13B to 70B models, customers push both chat and embedding workloads. We run an internal fleet of H100-ish cards and a lot of A100 equivalents in our racks. Our typical seq len is between 128-1024 depending on app.
[01:05] Diego: we're also doing a lot of fine-tuned models for verticals, and latency is a big selling point - we promise sub-200ms p50 for small chats in certain SKUs.
[01:20] Priya: ok good. that's helpful. on Redwood's side we support hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; for partners we often talk about dedicated capacity or private control plane deployed in a VPC. Does Arclight prefer a managed control plane or something customer-operated?
[01:40] Jordan: we want options. For some enterprise customers we need VPC or on-prem control, others are fine with a hosted control plane. Security demands vary—Sofia here handles compliance.
[01:52] Sofia: yes, we need SOC two evidence, KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and SSO/SAML for RBAC. Also some customers require data residency.
[02:05] Alex: totally, we've got templates for SOC 2 and KMS integrations, and Redwood Private can be deployed behind customer VPCs with KMS/HSM integration. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:20] Maya: what does integration look like—are you expecting us to upstream a custom runtime or just be an infra partner?
[02:30] Priya: can be multiple paths. 1) Redwood verifies your hardware profiles and we add you to our partner catalog, routing policy sends compatible inference to your pool. 2) you host Redwood Private in your region for customers that want the managed control plane locally. 3) for go-to-market we can also do joint benchmarks and case studies.
[02:52] Jordan: routing policy meaning we can take certain routes for latency-sensitive customers and fallback to hosted?
[03:00] Priya: yes, you can set policies by latency, cost, or region and fallbacks to other tiers. we also can choose quantized model variants to save cost; that might help with your capacity economics.
[03:15] Diego: curious about KV cache and batching—our customers want low p99 tails. how does Redwood handle KV cache for long chat state?
[03:30] Priya: we maintain KV cache at runtime and do continuous batching with smart eviction. sometimes transcripts say KV cash, sorry speech to text. but in practice it's per-request prefix caching and memory-managed kvs. For p99 tails we recommend small batch sizes for latency SLAs and prefix caching for repeated prompts.
[03:55] Jordan: ok. one challenge is our orchestration—we run Kubernetes with custom device plugins. Would Redwood Dedicated run on top of k8s or do we need to host a separate infra?
[04:10] Priya: Redwood Dedicated can be integrated with k8s; runtime is GPU-optimized but can be run as container workloads with our runtime image or via a lightweight agent. For partners it's common to validate kernel selection, quantization paths, and ensure the operator matches.
[04:30] Alex: on the business side, are you looking for an upstream partner to refer customers, or to resell Redwood as part of your stack?
[04:40] Maya: both. We want a partner agreement for referrals and also evaluate bundling Redwood Dedicated as an option customers can purchase.
[04:50] Diego: pricing and SLAs—what's typical for Dedicated?
[04:56] Alex: typically reserved capacity with monthly commits, SLA-backed latency/uptime, and options for burst capacity. We'll share a pricing template; for partners we can discuss margin on resells.
[05:10] Jordan: tech deep dive—we'd like to run a benchmark. what's the recommended pilot?
[05:18] Priya: recommend a 2-week pilot: 1) run inference at your site with a 1-2 model set (13B and 70B quantized variant), 2) measure throughput, p50/p95/p99, token cost, and 3) run routing/failover scenarios. We'll need model artifacts or references and a small dataset of prompts.
[05:42] Sofia: security review — what logs do you expose, and can audit logs be shipped to our SIEM?
[05:50] Priya: yes audit logs can be exported; we support forwarding to common SIEMs, and we have role-based access controls. KMS integrations for customer-managed keys are supported.
[06:05] Jordan: capacity: roughly per rack we run 8x H100-ish. average utilization varies but peaks around 70% during batch windows. can Redwood's scheduling respect rack-level placement?
[06:20] Priya: we can target placement by label and have routing policies to prefer certain pools. We may need a short integration to map your topology into our control plane.
[06:35] Alex: any hard blockers on procurement or legal?
[06:40] Jordan: procurement will need standard MSA and some partner reseller agreement. Also customers expect indemnities for data, but nothing unusual.
[06:50] Diego: network egress—some of our customers are sensitive to cross-region egress costs. If we host the control plane locally does that reduce egress?
[07:00] Priya: yes, hosting the private control plane in-customer-region keeps traffic internal; routing policies can prefer local pools to avoid egress.
[07:12] Maya: what about model variants and quantization? if our infra is integer-quantized, will Redwood serve those variants?
[07:20] Priya: we support quantized profiles (int8/int4) and select kernels accordingly. we maintain model catalog entries with recommended quantization and kernels by hardware. For partner onboarding we do a model qualification pass.
[07:40] Jordan: great. on telemetry—what metrics will we get?
[07:46] Priya: token-level cost, throughput, latency percentiles, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks. We can add custom metrics for your fleet.
[08:00] Jordan: any reference partners we can talk to?
[08:05] Alex: we can provide a couple of contacts, including a cloud GPU partner and a reseller. We'll include references in the partner packet.
[08:15] Sofia: timeline—our security team needs initial docs this week if possible.
[08:20] Alex: yes we'll push the SOC2/KMS pack right after the call.
[08:25] Priya: for the pilot I'll outline infra reqs: container runtime, device plugin, recommended kernel builds, and small runbook for throughput tests.
[08:35] Jordan: perfect. on go-to-market: joint webinars and co-marketing could help us.
[08:40] Maya: agreed, we'll draft a basic GTM plan after we validate tech.
[08:45] Tom: just to note, we also have a partner catalog workflow and verification checklist — once you pass model qualification we surface you in the catalog with verified performance badges.
[09:00] Alex: ok wrapping — recap of next steps: Alex send deck & security pack, Priya send pilot runbook, Jordan share fleet details, Sofia to compile security questions. follow up tech deep dive target week of 4/13.
[09:20] Jordan: sounds good thanks everyone.
[09:25] Alex: thanks, we'll email notes and next steps.

(Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts: 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'SOC two' for SOC2, and speaker attribution may shift in places.)
